chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrour, may Allah have mercy upon him, narrated to us; he said: A number of our companions narrated to me from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said:
He who sits with the people of doubt/suspicion is himself suspicious/doubtful.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الرَّيْبِ: People of doubt or suspicion; those characterized by uncertainty or wavering in faith/knowledge
key_terms.جَالَسَ: Sat with; implies regular or prolonged association
key_terms.مُرِيبٌ: Suspicious or doubtful; one who is characterized by rayb (doubt/suspicion)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sitting with people of doubt according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Sifat al-Shia, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this concise maxim to define the spiritual contagion of doubt, emphasizing that prolonged association with 'ahl al-rayb' (those of doubt' inevitably transfers their uncertainty to the observer. This principle underscores the Shia emphasis on purifying one's social circle to maintain doctrinal clarity and spiritual integrity, serving as a practical guideline for avoiding intellectual and moral corruption.
